title: Evaporating Cloud Input
description: Input schema for cloud_builder.py and assumption_analyzer.py

objective.description: Box A — the shared goal both sides of the conflict want to achieve

need_a.description: Box B — first condition necessary to achieve the objective

need_b.description: Box C — second condition also necessary to achieve the objective

want_a.description: Box D — what satisfies Need B (one side's position in the conflict)

want_b.description: Box D' — what satisfies Need C (the conflicting position)

assumptions.description: Hidden assumptions behind each arrow of the cloud

statement.description: The assumption stated as a falsifiable claim

type.description: Category of assumption — determines base vulnerability score

evidence_for.description: Evidence or reasoning supporting this assumption (used by assumption_analyzer.py)

evidence_against.description: Evidence or observations that challenge this assumption

examined.description: Has this assumption been explicitly questioned before? Default false = unexamined

examples.objective: Build a financially sustainable, growing business
examples.need_a: Generate enough revenue to scale operations
examples.need_b: Maintain positive cash flow and financial stability
examples.want_b: Minimize spending and preserve cash reserves

assumptions.statement: Revenue growth requires proportional increases in headcount and marketing spend
assumptions.evidence_for: Historical data shows headcount growth has tracked revenue growth
assumptions.evidence_against: SaaS benchmarks show best-in-class companies grow revenue faster than headcount

assumptions.statement: We cannot grow revenue through existing customers without new investment
assumptions.evidence_against: Expansion revenue from existing customers currently represents 0% of our growth

assumptions.statement: Our current cost structure does not allow for any reduction in revenue per unit
assumptions.evidence_for: Finance model shows break-even requires current pricing
assumptions.evidence_against: Fixed costs could be spread over more units if volume increased
